questions.q: Which of these is one of the four harm categories Azure AI Content Safety screens for?
questions.explain: The four harm categories are hate and fairness, sexual, violence, and self-harm.

questions.q: What does Prompt Shields specifically detect?
options: Jailbreak attempts and indirect (hidden document-based) attacks
questions.explain: Prompt Shields provides a unified API addressing jailbreak attacks (users trying to bypass safety rules) and indirect attacks (malicious instructions hidden in documents the model processes).

questions.q: What severity score corresponds to "Safe" content in Content Safety's four-level system?
questions.explain: The four severity levels are Safe (0), Low (2), Medium (4), and High (6).

questions.q: What does the View Code button do on the Analyze text/image content pages?
options: Exports a ready-to-use code sample matching your tested configuration and thresholds
Downloads a video recording of the test
questions.explain: View Code exports the exact call, including configured severity thresholds, so you can drop it directly into your application.

questions.q: What extra setup is needed to moderate an image by blob URL instead of uploading bytes directly?
options: Nothing — blob URLs work identically to uploaded bytes with no setup
The image must be converted to a PDF first
You must disable all content filtering first
The Content Safety resource needs a Storage Blob Data Reader role via managed identity
questions.explain: Analyzing an image by blob URL requires granting the Content Safety resource's managed identity a Storage Blob Data Reader (or higher) role on the storage account.
